title: Two Integral Sliding-Window Inequalities for Maximal Convolutions
summary: We prove two sliding-window inequalities for maximal convolutions. The first concerns the multiplicative maximal convolution. If $f$ and $g$ are nonnegative continuous functions on $[0,A]$ and $[0,B]$, respectively, define \[ h(x)=\max_{\substack{0\le u\le A\\0\le x-u\le B}} f(u)g(x-u),\qquad 0\le x\le A+B. \] Then there exists a window $[a,a+B]$ of length $B$ such that \[ \frac1B\int_a^{a+B}h(x)\,dx\ge \left(\frac1A\int_0^A f(x)\,dx\right) \left(\frac1B\int_0^B g(x)\,dx\right). \] The second concerns the additive maximal convolution.
